title: Domain-Specific SAEs vs General SAEs for Niche Harm Detection

original_idea.body:
# Domain-Specific SAEs vs General SAEs for Niche Harm Detection

**Problem:** Domain-specific SAEs can capture features general SAEs miss; for niche high-stakes harm domains, general SAEs may lack a clean feature, creating monitoring blind spots.

**Direction:** Compare a general-corpus SAE against features on a narrow domain corpus for a niche-harm concept; measure how much the general SAE misses.

**Why it matters:** Monitoring built on general SAEs may have predictable gaps in the high-stakes long tail.

**Relevant context:** arXiv 2508.09363; SAELens; public domain corpora.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (general-SAE blind spots in high-stakes domains) but indirect catastrophic-risk link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: May need to train a domain SAE; intermediate ML fundamentals.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on one niche-harm concept comparison; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Diffuse evaluation work, public corpora; lab-independent.

low_compute.reasoning: Possible domain-SAE training + feature search; single mid GPU days.

novelty.reasoning: Domain-specific SAE benefit is shown generally; the niche-harm monitoring-gap angle may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Domain-SAE benefits are shown; the niche-harm blind-spot measurement may be open.
